ambiguous: hooks/interventions are simultaneously the Decision surface (they veto tool calls) and the Approval machinery (interrupt/Confirm pauses) — the same code authors both layers; a manifest must not count one hook as evidence for two layers
Bedrock Guardrails sit on the model channel (input/output content redaction) and are neither Decision nor Approval for tool execution, despite the name
legacy tools-package consent prompts (shell/file_write/python_repl) are a tool-internal approval surface, distinct from the SDK's hook/interrupt approval machinery

sandbox: an optional Agent(sandbox=...) routing (e.g. DockerSandbox) and the AgentCore code_interpreter tool exist, but no sandbox is part of the core SDK's tool execution; confinement semantics unestablished at the pin — not asserted
layer_vocabulary.notes: No rules layer exists: there is no declarative per-command policy surface in the SDK core, so 'rules' is NOT covered. Decision lives in hook/intervention Python code executed in-process before tool execution (BeforeToolCallEvent.cancel_tool / selected_tool / tool_use mutation; InterventionHandler returning Proceed/Deny/Guide/Confirm/Transform). Approval: interrupts (event.interrupt -> stop_reason 'interrupt' -> interruptResponse resume), the vended HumanInTheLoop intervention (Confirm action; stdio/custom ask; allowed_tools; LLM classifier; trust in agent.state), and legacy tools' own consent prompts (BYPASS_TOOL_CONSENT / STRANDS_NON_INTERACTIVE). Effect: tools execute in-process on the host with the process's privileges by default; optional sandbox routing or the AgentCore code_interpreter tool are separate configurations, not defaults.

measurement_route_evidence: No vendor-confirmed checker exists and no declarative rule semantics exist to reconstruct: the Decision surface is arbitrary Python hook/intervention code executed in-process (DOC: Hooks, Interventions, strandsagents.com, retrieved 2026-10-22). (INFERENCE on DOC+REPRO)

policy_ingestion.defaults: No gate registered -> the tool call proceeds to execution (intervention methods default to Proceed(); hooks/interventions are opt-in). There is no no-match state in the harness; our reporter serializes 'no gate decided' as unknown, never allow (INV-005).
policy_ingestion.surface: none — no declarative policy surface; Decision lives in hook code (HookProvider callbacks on BeforeToolCallEvent) and intervention handlers (strands.interventions.InterventionHandler) supplied in Python at Agent construction. Substitutes: vended CedarAuthorization intervention (Cedar policy strings/.cedar files, default-deny, evaluated in-process at the tool boundary); Bedrock Guardrails config on BedrockModel (model input/output content only — not a tool-action policy).

spike_answers.a_native_oracle: NO. Strands is a Python library, not a CLI harness: no binary, no check/evaluate/dry-run entrypoint, no policy file whose decision for a command could be queried offline. The decision for a tool call is produced at runtime by user Python code in the agent loop (a BeforeToolCallEvent hook setting cancel_tool, or an intervention handler returning Deny/Confirm/Proceed).
spike_answers.b_documented_semantics: NO for the harness's Decision layer. A reconstructed route needs documented semantics of a rule surface; Strands' gate is arbitrary Python — the docs specify the event contract precisely (mutable properties, firing points, ordering; intervention actions and precedence deny > confirm > guide > transform > proceed) but cannot specify what any given policy hook decides. The documented contract does support the Approval-layer configured route (A2) and an auditable reference-agent design; it does not support Decision-layer reconstruction.
spike_answers.c_surface_record: Surface: Python SDK — Agent(tools=[...], hooks=[HookProvider...], interventions=[InterventionHandler...], model=BedrockModel by default). No policy config file exists in the core SDK. Defaults: with no hook/intervention registered, a model-emitted tool call proceeds to execution (intervention default Proceed()); there is no no-match state — absence of a gate is execution, serialized by our reporter as unknown, never allow. Substitutes recorded: vended CedarAuthorization intervention (declarative Cedar policies, default-deny, in-process at the tool boundary — not an offline oracle); Bedrock Guardrails on BedrockModel (screens model inputs/outputs only, never tool actions). NO verdicts issued; measurement route is 'no paper surface' and the FinePrint target is an instrumented reference agent measured at the Approval (A3 interrupt) and Effect (E1/E2) layers.
